- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment > 0.7 → forecast rises too fast).  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model fails to correct downward quickly — overshoots and lags mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is low (e.g., <0.3), model underestimates true price drops, missing downward momentum.  
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices unless sentiment is strongly bearish or volatile.  
- Model exhibits “lagging” behavior — true price turns often occur 1–2 days before forecast adjusts, especially after sentiment shifts.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated high values (e.g., 0.8+), model should reduce forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.  
- When true price drops sharply after a spike, model often fails to recognize the “reversion” phase — underestimates the depth of correction.
